card.problem_text:
Cook's membrane (linear elasticity, compressible and nearly incompressible), SWG method on polygonal meshes.
Geometry: A 2D tapered plate (Cook's membrane), shown in Fig. 10.4. The text gives no vertex coordinates. It gives only the evaluation point Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right end. No thickness or plane-strain/plane-stress assumption is stated.
Material: Linear isotropic elasticity, not hyperelastic. Case 1: E = 1, nu = 1/3. Case 2 (nearly incompressible): E = 1.12499998125, nu = 0.499999975. The reference value applies to case 2 only.
Boundary conditions: Clamped on one end (the left end, by inference from Q being on the right end). A shear traction acts on the opposite end. The remaining edges are presumably traction-free, but the text does not say so.
Loading: Shear traction g = (0, 1/16) on the end opposite the clamp. The text does not say whether it is distributed uniformly or is a resultant.
Discretisation in the paper: The reference value 16.442 is taken from [2, 22]. Its mesh, element type and element count are not stated in this section. (The paper's own SWG runs use triangle, quadrilateral, hexagonal and octagonal partitions, e.g. h = 1/16. Those are the method under test, not the reference.)
Features: The corners where the clamped end meets the traction-free top and bottom edges give a corner singularity in the continuum stress. This is made more severe by near-incompressibility.; The corners where the end carrying the shear traction meets the free edges. With a smooth traction distribution, these give no strong singularity. The load distribution is not stated..
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: Vertical displacement at Q (Vertical displacement u2 at Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right end. Case 2 (nu = 0.499999975).); Relative error of tip displacement vs reference, all mesh types (Relative difference between the computed u2(Q) and 16.442, as a function of total DOF for each polygonal mesh type); Displacement and pseudo-pressure fields (Contour plots of the deformed shape coloured by pseudo-pressure (kappa = 1), and contour plots of u1 and u2 for kappa = 1 and kappa = 0 on the quadrilateral mesh with h = 1/16)?

spec.name: Cook's membrane, linear elasticity (compressible nu=1/3 and nearly incompressible nu=0.499999975), SWG method on polygonal meshes: tip vertical displacement u2(Q) compared with the literature reference 16.442
spec.geometry: 2D tapered plate (Cook's membrane, paper Fig. 10.4). The text gives no vertex coordinates. The only coordinate given is the evaluation point Q = (48, 52), stated to be the midpoint of the right end, so the right end is the vertical segment x = 48 centred at y = 52. The left end is clamped (inferred). The top and bottom edges are inclined and presumably traction-free. Thickness and the plane-strain/plane-stress assumption are not stated.
spec.material: Linear isotropic elasticity (small strain), not hyperelastic. Case 1: E = 1, nu = 1/3 (compressible). Case 2: E = 1.12499998125, nu = 0.499999975 (nearly incompressible, so lambda/mu is very large and low-order displacement elements can lock). The reference value 16.442 applies to case 2 only. The paper uses a pseudo-pressure variable and a parameter kappa in {0, 1}. What kappa means (formulation variant or stabilisation) is not defined in the excerpt.
spec.loading: Shear traction g = (0, 1/16) on the right end x = 48. The edge opposite the clamp is the right end by inference. The text does not say whether g is a uniform traction density or whether it stands for a total resultant. The left end is fully clamped (u = 0). The top and bottom edges are presumably traction-free (not stated). No body force is mentioned. The load is static and linear, so there are no limit points or load-level issues.
qois: u2(Q): vertical displacement at Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right end, for case 2 (nu = 0.499999975), compared with the reference 16.442 from [2, 22]. This is a pointwise displacement far from the clamped-corner singularities. For a locking-free discretisation it converges under refinement (for a uniform load it is the midpoint of a smooth edge). It is a usable QoI, but the reference can only be trusted if [2, 22] report a converged refinement study under the same BCs, load distribution and plane assumption.

Relative error |u2_h(Q) - 16.442| / 16.442 against total DOF for each polygonal mesh type (triangle, quadrilateral, hexagonal, octagonal). This is a derived quantity. It can only resolve errors larger than the error of the reference itself, so the curves will level off at about the reference's own accuracy (unknown: 16.442 is given to 5 significant figures, i.e. about 1e-4 relative at best). Rates read from it are not trustworthy beyond that point. Because of the corner singularities, the observed rates will be below the smooth-solution rates.

Displacement fields u1 and u2 and the pseudo-pressure field (deformed shape coloured by pseudo-pressure for kappa = 1, plus u1 and u2 contours for kappa = 1 and kappa = 0) on the quadrilateral mesh with h = 1/16. These are qualitative only. The displacement contours can be checked for smoothness and for the absence of locking or checkerboarding. The pseudo-pressure, like the stress, is singular at the clamped-free corners, so its peak values do not converge and cannot be a reference. Away from the corners it could be compared through region averages, but the paper gives no reference field values.
well_posedness: Dirichlet condition: the left end is fully clamped (u = 0). This removes rigid-body modes, so the linear elastic problem has a unique solution as long as the clamp has positive length.

Material stability: the linear isotropic material with E > 0 and -1 < nu < 0.5 is strongly elliptic and coercive in both cases. For case 2, nu = 0.499999975 is very close to 0.5, so the problem is nearly incompressible. Only locking-free or mixed discretisations (the SWG pseudo-pressure formulation is meant to be one) converge uniformly in lambda. For a locking discretisation, u2(Q) will be far too small on practical meshes.
Loading: linear static problem with no geometric or material nonlinearity, so there are no limit points or bifurcations, and the solution scales linearly with g.

Singular features: where the clamped left end meets the traction-free top and bottom edges, the stress and pressure are singular (near-incompressibility makes it worse). So the peak stress or peak pseudo-pressure at those corners does not converge. Energy, displacements (including u2(Q)) and region averages away from the corners do converge, at reduced rates set by the corner singularity exponent.
Corners at the loaded end: for a uniform traction no strong singularity is expected, but the traction distribution is not stated. A non-smooth or point-like load would add a singularity near Q.

Reference consistency: 16.442 is only valid if [2, 22] used the same geometry, the same plane assumption (plane strain vs plane stress gives different results for the nu = 0.4999 case), the same traction distribution and the same thickness. None of these are confirmed in the text.
Case 1 (nu = 1/3) has no reference value given. It can only be checked through a self-convergence (mesh refinement) study.
open_questions: Vertex coordinates of the membrane are not given. The usual Cook geometry is consistent with Q = (48, 52), but the text does not state it.
Plane strain or plane stress? Thickness? The text states neither, and both change u2(Q) for the nearly incompressible case.
Is g = (0, 1/16) a uniform traction density on the right end, or a total shear force (resultant) spread in some other way?
Are the top and bottom edges traction-free? This is presumed but not stated.
Is the clamped end the left end (x = 0 side)? This is inferred only from Q being on the right end.

How was the reference 16.442 from [2, 22] obtained: element type, mesh family, number of DOF, whether it was extrapolated, and its estimated error? The element enum value 'Q4' and reference type 'mesh_refinement_family' are placeholders. The SWG polygonal method under test is not in the element enum, and the excerpt does not specify the reference discretisation.
What is the parameter kappa (0 vs 1)? How is the pseudo-pressure defined (e.g. -lambda div u, or a scaled variant)?
Is there any reference value for case 1 (nu = 1/3)? Only case 2 is covered by 16.442.
Is u2(Q) evaluated at the node at Q, or interpolated? The SWG approximation may be discontinuous, so it may matter which element trace is used.

sources.quote: It gives only the evaluation point Q = (48, 52), the midpoint of the right end.
Shear traction g = (0, 1/16) on the end opposite the clamp.
The reference value 16.442 is taken from [2, 22].

assumptions: The vertex coordinates aren't stated. I used the standard Cook's membrane geometry (0,0), (48,44), (48,60), (0,44). This fits the given Q = (48,52), which is the midpoint of the right edge x=48 between y=44 and y=60. That edge has length 16, which also fits g = 1/16 giving a unit total shear force. If the paper's Fig. 10.4 is different, this model is wrong.

The text names no plane condition. I chose plane strain, because nu -> 0.5 near-incompressibility is a plane-strain (or 3D) concept and plane stress would remove the volumetric constraint. Thickness is taken as 1.

I applied g = (0, 1/16) as a uniform traction per unit length on the right edge, not as a resultant. This matches the standard Cook's membrane setup and the reference 16.442. The text doesn't say so explicitly.
The clamp is on the left edge x=0, inferred from Q lying on the right end.
The top and bottom inclined edges are traction-free. The text says 'presumably' but does not confirm it.
Only case 2 is modelled (E = 1.12499998125, nu = 0.499999975), because the reference value applies to case 2 only. Case 1 (E = 1, nu = 1/3) would be the same description with those constants.

Trustworthiness: u2(Q) is a displacement, a global quantity. It converges under refinement despite the singularities at the clamped corners (0,0) and (0,44), so it can serve as a reference value if a locking-free discretisation is refined to convergence. At nu = 0.499999975, standard displacement-based Q4/Q9 elements will lock and underestimate u2(Q) badly, so the pipeline must use a mixed or locking-free formulation or a strongly refined higher-order mesh. The quoted 16.442 comes from [2, 22] with an unstated mesh and element. It is a literature value to compare against, not independently verified.

The relative-error-vs-DOF curves are derived from u2(Q) and 16.442. They are only as trustworthy as that reference: the 16.442 has 5 significant figures, so relative errors below about 1e-4 to 1e-5 can't be resolved. They show the method's convergence; they are not reference data in their own right.

The contour plots of u1 and u2 (displacement fields) are smooth and converge, but they are qualitative only. The pseudo-pressure field is singular at the clamped corners (0,0) and (0,44), and near-incompressibility makes this worse. Its peak values there don't converge under refinement, so pointwise or peak pressure from these plots can't serve as a trustworthy reference. Pressure away from the corners or averaged over regions can.
